text: Planning a trip can be as exciting as the journey itself. Before I visited Japan, I spent weeks researching train routes and booking traditional guesthouses, eager to experience something completely new. Once there, the culture amazed me—from serene temples to bustling markets. Trying local food was a highlight, though ordering was tricky; I once pointed at a picture only to receive a dish covered in a strange, spicy paste. Language barriers made simple tasks difficult, but smiles and gestures helped us connect. In the end, the imperfect moments became the best memories, reminding me that flexibility often leads to the most authentic adventures.
